author: AlexBair
quote:
Growing up, Ocarina of Time was literally one of my earliest gaming memories I played the original back when I was around three years old NA N64. Coming back to it now with this remake, I just wanted to take my time and soak it all in, and after 60 hours of exploring every corner of Hyrule, I can honestly say it hits almost every mark.
Everything that made the original magic is still intact here, just modernized in a way that actually respects the source material. The atmosphere, the dungeons, and the sense of adventure hold up completely, and stretching it out to a 60 hour playthrough felt natural rather than padded.
The only thing holding it back for me is the voice acting. Having full voices in a world I've known in my head since I was a kid felt a tad bit uncanny at times, and some deliveries didn't quite land the way I imagined them. Also replayed with the japanese VA. With the original VA for navi, I felt right at home

author: AlexBair
quote: Honestly, GTA 6 feels like a eh for me right now. I get why people give it a 9 for the sheer scale and detail, but the pacing kills the fun. It’s GTA, not Red Dead spending the opening hours doing slow errands, relationship upkeep, and grinding just to unlock basic sandbox features like cheats feels completely backwards. On top of the 30 FPS cap with dips, day-one GTA+ car perks, and the blurry anti-aliasing/upscaling on grass that literally strains my eyes especially when driving, it’s hard to overlook flaws that any other game would get hammered for. Map is nice dont get me wrong. But main story doesnt even use half the map
